questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “nucleophilic acyl substitution”?

options.label: A
options.text: A two-step addition-elimination reaction where a nucleophile attacks a carboxylic acid derivative, forming a tetrahedral intermediate that expels a leaving group.

options.label: B
options.text: A high-energy carboxylic acid derivative containing a sulfur atom bonded to an acyl group (R-CO-SR'), such as biological Acetyl-CoA.

options.label: C
options.text: A condensation reaction using dicyclohexylcarbodiimide to activate carboxylic acids for direct amide or peptide bond formation.

options.label: D
options.text: A carboxylic acid derivative formed from two acyl groups linked by a central oxygen atom (R-CO-O-CO-R').

questions.correct_answer: A two-step addition-elimination reaction where a nucleophile attacks a carboxylic acid derivative, forming a tetrahedral intermediate that expels a leaving group.
questions.explanation: A accurate description of nucleophilic acyl substitution is: A two-step addition-elimination reaction where a nucleophile attacks a carboxylic acid derivative, forming a tetrahedral intermediate that expels a leaving group.
